turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so let's start with who decided to put a zero in the gradebook, and when.
Owen talks about you in class, by the way.
I'm not here to be chatted up, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
He's one of the kindest kids I teach. He walked a new student around the building all through September.
Don't manage me, Hale. I'm sure he's kind, and it has nothing to do with a zero he found out about on his phone in the middle of class. Who decided, and was Owen heard first?
A kid like that doesn't cheat out of malice. He was overwhelmed. We can both agree on that, right?
No, we can't agree on that. My child never lies, and you just used the word "cheat" about him with nothing in your hand. Are you calling me a liar too, Hale?
